clue.text: Can get good start after escape — but not for long

indicators.note: after says the escape part comes before the rest in the answer

parts.note: to escape is to flee
a can is a tin

indicators.note: the start of the word good is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone escapes and finds a promising start, but it does not last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the noun; 'start' takes the opening letter of 'good', and 'after' sets the escape piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting is brief and passes quickly, lasting only a short time.

clue.text: Limp, round, very quiet insect around

indicators.note: around says the insect encloses the other letters

parts.note: a fly is an insect
O is round in shape
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A list of descriptions for a weak, round, silent bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' has the insect enclose the other letters; the musical marking for very quiet is pianissimo, written pp.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy means hanging loosely without stiffness, like a limp hat brim.

clue.text: Charm the last listener

parts.note: the end is the last part
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A final audience member is won over.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked, winning their affection.

clue.text: This is a twist, or is not if untwisted

indicators.note: untwisted asks for the letters of or is not to be undone and rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether something is twisted or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untwisted' rearranges OR IS NOT; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting an object about its axis.

clue.text: In hairs, tiny ones turning up?

definitions.text: In hairs, tiny ones turning up?

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
In tells us the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Little creatures are spotted in someone's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' finds STIN across 'hairS TINy', and 'turning up' reverses it; the whole clue also describes lice eggs found in hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Nits are the eggs of head lice, tiny things that cling to hair.

clue.text: Replacement called for — umpire indisposed

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a sports official like an umpire
indisposed means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A substitute official is summoned because the umpire has fallen sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A refill is a fresh supply put in place of one used up, so a substitute.

clue.text: Spring forth to give English fellow a note

parts.note: a fellow is a man
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An Englishman is given a musical note to come out with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give' is a link; TE is the tonic sol-fa note also written ti.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or issue from a source.

clue.text: Eric's nib is damaged — but write with it

indicators.note: is damaged suggests the letters of the nib phrase are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Eric's pen nib is broken but he still writes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is damaged' rearranges ERICSNIB; 'but' and 'with it' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to write or engrave words on a surface.

clue.text: Palm-tree flourished here in Wales

indicators.note: flourished means waved about, so the letters of palm-tree are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A palm tree once grew well in a corner of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourished' rearranges PALMTREE; LAMPETER is a small university town in west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampeter is a market town in Ceredigion, west Wales, a place there.

clue.text: A doubter can be hard to persuade

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of the phrase may be turned into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: Sceptics are notoriously difficult to win over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals rearranging the eight letters of A DOUBTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An obdurate person is stubborn and unyielding, not easily moved by argument.

clue.text: Managed accordingly, with male lead, for an extortionate fee

parts.note: managed, as in ran a business
so means accordingly, therefore

indicators.note: the lead of the word male is its first letter, at the front

explanation.surface: A business run by a man charges outrageous prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' takes the first letter of 'male'; 'for' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is a payment demanded under threat, typically for releasing a captive.

clue.text: His darts aimed at the bull

definitions.text: His darts aimed at the bull

parts.words: His darts aimed at the bull
parts.note: reads like a pub darts player going for the bullseye, but describes a mounted bullfighter's lances aimed at a real bull

explanation.surface: A darts player aims for the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the horseman in a bullfight who weakens the bull with a lance.

clue.text: Start pouring something corrosive on banks of lake — but it remains unruffled

indicators.note: on places the corrosive part next to the bank letter, following it
the start of the word pouring is its first letter
a bank is an edge of the lake, here taken as its opening letter only

parts.note: an acid is a corrosive substance

explanation.surface: Someone pours acid at the edge of a lake, yet the water stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' gives P from 'pouring'; 'banks of' gives just L, the first edge of 'lake'; 'on' sets ACID after it. 'but it remains' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid describes calm, still water or a temperament not easily disturbed.

clue.text: Be contrary, in saying a red is a green

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Calling a red a green is a fair way to pick an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to a run of letters spanning 'reD IS A GREEn'; 'saying a' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to take the opposite view, to be contrary in opinion.

clue.text: A first-rate cheese turned up, I found, in this place

indicators.note: found suggests the letter I is discovered sitting inside the reversed group
turned up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top
first picks the opening letter of the word rate

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Somebody discovers a fine cheese has appeared here.
explanation.walkthrough: A, R (first of 'rate') and EDAM, 'turned up', give MADERA; 'found' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, a location.

clue.text: A French chap with a frisky beagle — it has a will of its own!

definitions.text: it has a will of its own!

parts.note: un is the French for a
a chap is a man
taken as written

indicators.note: frisky suggests lively jumping about, so the letters of the dog breed are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Frenchman out with a lively beagle finds the dog will not be controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisky' rearranges the dog's six letters; UN is the French masculine indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a will of its own refuses control, which is exactly being impossible to handle.

clue.text: Port dues unfortunately began to grow

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of port dues are jumbled

explanation.surface: Harbour charges unhappily started to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges PORTDUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprouted means put out new shoots, starting to develop.

clue.text: Fir cones mutating — here's some evidence

indicators.note: mutating means changing form, so the letters of fir cones change order

explanation.surface: Changing fir cones provide scientific clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutating' rearranges FIRCONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic science supplies proof for courts, so the word signals courtroom evidence.

clue.text: Proceeds to the last tasks — making pastries

parts.note: proceeds are the profit from a sale

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word the

parts.note: roles are jobs or tasks

explanation.surface: Money earned goes on the final jobs of a baking order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes E, the final letter of 'the'; 'to' and 'making' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Profiteroles are small choux buns, usually cream-filled and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Very strong tin seen to buckle

indicators.note: to buckle means to bend out of shape, so the letters of tin seen are distorted

explanation.surface: A sturdy tin is seen to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to buckle' rearranges TINSEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means extreme in degree, forceful.

clue.text: Turned green?

parts.note: suggests something changing colour, but means becoming jealous, the green-eyed monster

explanation.definitionFit: Green is the colour associated with jealousy, so someone turned green is jealous.

clue.text: Fair attraction, despite their reputed losses

definitions.text: Fair attraction, despite their reputed losses

parts.words: Fair attraction, despite their reputed losses
parts.note: a funfair ride, with a nod to the saying that what is lost on one ride is gained on the roundabouts

explanation.surface: A fairground ride stays popular even though it supposedly loses money.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'what you lose on the swings you gain on the roundabouts' means losses balance out.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's fairground rides that sway back and forth are a classic fair attraction.

clue.text: A yell rising at first sight of these marbles

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the word yell reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word sight

explanation.surface: Someone shouts on first spotting a set of marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns YELL into LLEY; 'first' gives S from 'sight'; 'at' and 'of these' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are large playing marbles, traditionally made of alabaster.

clue.text: Proposal is noted?

explanation.surface: A suggestion gets written down.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: a piece of music written in notes is literally noted.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is both an opening offer in a negotiation and an orchestral prelude written out in musical notation.

clue.text: Retrograde law over sound maintenance

annotationWithheld.why: Retrograde law over sound maintenance (6): reversed LAW gives WAL, but no reading of 'over sound' supplies AVO (reversing everything needs LAW + O + VA), and no source found for the intended parse

clue.text: Pool part of income revenue

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A swimming pool brings in part of someone's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span 'incoME REvenue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake or pond, a still body of water.

clue.text: Drink, appearing sober after knocking it back

indicators.note: after puts the sober part following the turned word
knocking back together say the word it is turned round to read the other way
back completes knocking back, telling us the word it is turned round

parts.note: sober means sane, clear-headed

explanation.surface: After downing a drink, someone still seems sober.
explanation.walkthrough: The split indicator 'knocking ... back' turns the little word round; 'after' places the sober piece behind it; 'appearing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an herbal tea, a hot infusion taken as a beverage.

clue.text: Animal going to earth after attack

indicators.note: going to says the animal joins up following the lair

parts.note: an earth is a fox's lair, a den
an ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A hunted creature dashes for cover after being attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, and an earth is a fox's burrow; 'going to' attaches the animal behind the lair, and 'after' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, a verbal assault on someone.

clue.text: One who cuts off, when at work?

explanation.walkthrough: To dock a tail is to cut it short; the second definition plays on a dock worker being at the docks when working.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names both someone who trims tails short and a port labourer whose workplace is the quayside.

clue.text: Keeps on despite having second thoughts about maltreated sister

indicators.note: about means placed around the other piece

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

indicators.note: maltreated means badly handled, so the letters of sister are knocked about

explanation.surface: Someone carries on regardless after having doubts over a sister being abused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maltreated' scrambles the sibling's letters, and 'about' wraps the postscript round them; 'despite having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue steadily despite difficulty.
